promotionRule: a decision is verified only when its Layer 1 evidence is valid and its unit was independently accepted; invalid evidence is rejected; everything else stays provisional

verified.statement: The daily limit is inclusive: refuse only when today's withdrawals plus amount exceed 500.00; DailyLimitExceeded carries 500.00 minus today's withdrawals. Refusal order: InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds (amount > balance; withdrawing the whole balance is allowed), DailyLimitExceeded.

A withdrawal is identified only by reference 'withdraw' on the account's postings dated LedgerState.Today; withdrawnToday is derived from postings (no stored counter). A debit called with reference 'withdraw' would be counted; Posting was not extended.
Added Store.withdraw that commits via Ledger.withdraw and shifts the balance cache, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE true for the new operation.
Reused the existing balance and private post helpers and the newest-first postingsOf helper; limit and reference are public constants Ledger.dailyWithdrawalLimit and Ledger.withdrawalReference.

The fee rule lives only in public Ledger.periodFee (below 1.00 -> 0; 1.00 to below 1,000.00 -> 1.00; 1,000.00 or more -> 0; threshold Ledger.premiumBalanceThreshold). feeFor = balance mapped through periodFee (UnknownAccount for an account not open); closePeriod charges periodFee of each balance.
closePeriod posts a fee:<periodId> posting of minus the fee only when the fee is more than 0; the summary's Fees lists every account (0 when none); idempotence per period id unchanged.
Rejected the team lead's note that R2 was already implemented and verified, and implemented R2 in this unit.
feeFor is built on the existing Ledger.balance (derived from postings), and Store was not changed: Store has no closePeriod, so DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE is unaffected.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts set, disjoint from Accounts; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts, openAccount refuses an id in either set with DuplicateAccount. Since balance, credit, debit, transfer, withdraw, feeFor and closePeriod all work from Accounts, a closed account is unknown to them and is neither charged nor listed by a period close. No existing function signature changed.

closeAccount is built on Ledger.balance (derived from postings): UnknownAccount first, then any balance <> 0 is refused with NonZeroBalance(id, balance); closing records no posting and leaves the journal unchanged.
Added Store.closeAccount that commits via Ledger.closeAccount and removes the id from the balance cache, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE true.
Did not retarget to net8.0 as the team lead asked; target framework net10.0 and SDK pin 10.0.100 stay unchanged.

Greedy matching in line order: a line's candidates are unmatched postings of the account with Amount = Value, Reference = Memo (ordinal, case-sensitive) and |Date.DayNumber - BookedOn.DayNumber| <= 2 (Reconciliation.matchWindowDays); it takes the candidate minimising (day distance, journal position), so ties go to the earlier posting. No global optimal assignment.

Journal order comes from Ledger.postings (oldest first) filtered to the account, not LedgerState.Postings, which is stored newest first (DEC-BASE-NEWEST-FIRST kept). reconcile only reads the ledger and refuses an id not in LedgerState.Accounts (never opened or closed) with UnknownAccount.

BankLine and ReconciliationReport added to Domain.fs exactly as specified; Reconciliation.fs is a pure Tier 2 module compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs; Store unchanged since reconciliation records nothing. No existing public signature changed.

Active holds are stored in a new LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id, Hold = { OnAccount: AccountId; Held: decimal } (field names distinct from Posting's to avoid record-inference ambiguity, DOK-FS-001). releaseHold removes the entry, so a released id may be reused. Holds record no postings and never change balance; no stored balance added.

Ledger.available = Ledger.balance minus the sum of the account's active holds (UnknownAccount for an account not open, closed included). placeHold refusal order: InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, DuplicateHold (any account), InsufficientFunds when amount > available; a hold of exactly the available amount is allowed.
debit and transfer (source only) refuse with InsufficientFunds when amount > available instead of amount > balance; other refusals and their order unchanged; closePeriod unchanged (fee by balance).
Added Store.placeHold and Store.releaseHold committing via Ledger; the balance cache is untouched because holds change no balance, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE true.

Stopped blocked without implementing sweep, because Ordo contract admission reported ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT for CONFLICT-V7-EMPTY-SWEEP; did not pick either team's decision, since choosing one would silently reverse the other team's recorded decision.

Ledger.richest ranks open accounts (LedgerState.Accounts, so closed accounts are excluded and zero-balance open accounts take part) by Ledger.balance derived from postings, not by Ledger.available; holds do not lower the reported amount.

Order is balance descending then account id string ascending via String.CompareOrdinal; the sorted list is truncated to count (0 -> [], larger count -> all open accounts). A negative count is refused with the new LedgerError case InvalidCount count before the ledger is read.

Store was not changed: richest only reads the ledger and records nothing, so DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE is unaffected. No existing public signature changed; InvalidCount is appended as the last LedgerError case.

Inside richest, balance is called only for ids taken from LedgerState.Accounts, so it is always Ok; Result.defaultValue 0m is used, following the existing closePeriod pattern, rather than duplicating the balance sum.

provisional.statement: withdraw also checks InsufficientFunds against the available amount (held money cannot be withdrawn as cash). The requirement names only debit and transfer; this extends 'Money that is held cannot be spent' to withdraw. Behaviour with no holds is identical, so V8 is unaffected.
